correctness.rationale: For a c0-sum of compact-operator algebras, the standard quotient embeds densely by right multiplication with the square root of the state density into the indicated Hilbert–Schmidt direct sum. It is onto exactly when the support projection has finitely many finite-rank blocks. Under that condition the support corner is finite dimensional and faithful, so every module quotient is isomorphic to the closed range obtained by multiplying by the support projection. In the commutative case the standard quotient is the image of continuous functions in the corresponding L2 space; closedness forces finite measure support by the bounded inverse theorem and disjoint bump functions, while finite support gives a finite direct sum of fibers for every module. The explicit infinite-support counterexamples therefore independently refute the unrestricted abstract wording.

originality.rationale: The Abedi–Moslehian primary abstract explicitly states arbitrary-state completeness for compact-operator and commutative algebras, but the audited counterexamples show that statement cannot be correct as written. Resultary and web searches did not locate the two sharp finite-support classifications or the explicit Hilbert–Schmidt completion model in independent prior work. The article's full text was unavailable: direct arXiv PDF transport failed, the publisher page required subscription, and lawful full-text retrieval attempts did not yield a verified PDF. That inaccessible plausible source is recorded as a residual risk rather than silently treated as novelty evidence.

value.rationale: This is a sharp repair of a published completeness statement: it identifies exactly which mixed states survive, gives a concrete completion model, and shows that infinite support already fails on the standard module. The boundary is mathematically natural and directly motivated by the source's claimed scope.
